title: Australia's Grid Transition: What 25 Years of NEM Data Reveals
summary: Twenty-five years of NEM data show that Australia's transition is changing generation, timing, carbon intensity and price formation at different speeds.
key_takeaway: Renewable growth has changed the generation mix; the decisive next step is coordinating transmission, storage, flexible demand and market design around it.

inline_figures.caption: Monthly distributions reveal different seasonal signatures for coal, wind, hydro, solar and other generation sources.
Carbon intensity differs sharply across generation sources, so a change in output is not equivalent to a change in emissions.
Emissions and average market price have a weak, changing relationship across the record.
Rolling growth rates show mature thermal generation changing slowly while newer renewable sources expand from a smaller base.
A large-format synthesis board that brings the article's five principal pieces of evidence into one readable argument.
